transcript: I went back down to Greenwich last night to see Creditors, the other play being presented in repertory at the Minetta Lane Theatre. I think I liked this one even more than Sexual Misconduct of the Middle Classes because this one really kept me guessing. It's a slow burn with three characters: an artist, a novelist, and a teacher. Honestly, it might be best to not know anything else going into it, but I'll just say that this is a fascinating moral and psychological piece about narratives. It's about the narratives we create about ourselves, each other, and our relationships, and the ways that those narratives impact our self-perceptions. You’re kind of forced to evaluate and reevaluate these characters as the play progresses, and you may realize by the end that you're just as malleable and manipulable as they are. The performances from Liev Schreiber, Maggie Siff, and Justice Smith are really great, and this story, in its modern adaptation by Jen Silverman, feels fresh and alive in this intimate theater. The audience I was in was quite reactive with each turn and revelation which made it all the more exciting of an experience. As tickets for this are as low as $35 at the box office and through digital lottery, I would absolutely recommend trying to catch either or both these plays that are running here. With that, another program for my collection.
